column1: # Enterprise control map — the machine-readable source of truth (#874).
# One row per rule in Part B of docs/GOLDEN-RULES.md (the platform/SaaS spine).
# `scripts/check-control-coverage.sh` validates every row against the repository:
#   * the rule exists in the spine's Part B;
#   * every module path exists;
#   * every control named is INVOKED BY A GATE. A control is either a check script
#     (discovered by scripts/discover-checks.sh, or named in scripts/verify.sh / the
#     Makefile) or a SUITE, written `suite:<dir>` — and a suite counts only when
#     scripts/pytest-suites.txt DECLARES it, because that manifest is what
#     scripts/run-pytest-suites.sh executes. A control nobody runs is a formality.
#   * a rule that is not ENFORCED is recorded in scripts/control-coverage-gaps.tsv,
#     which is SHRINK-ONLY: a new gap is refused by name.
# Status vocabulary — the honest three, not a pass/fail:
#   ENFORCED  a gate control exists whose STATED SUBJECT is this rule
#   PARTIAL   a control covers part of the rule, and the remainder is a gap
#   GAP       no gate control enforces it today
# Format: <rule>\t<status>\t<modules (comma-separated)>\t<controls (comma-separated, "-" for none)>
# `rule` is the spine rule id; the subject is the spine's own heading, never
# restated here, so the two cannot drift apart. The `rule status modules controls`
# line below is a HEADER, not a row — it is commented out on purpose, and the gate
# additionally requires a row's first field to look like a rule id.
